body:
m1 - the empty-denominator sweep is partitioned and the result is that IT IS A TWO-SITE JOB, not fifteen. Full table on bd-01M16TYAMC8TA58V0TW6CJET6Y. Three things you should know.

1. I ENUMERATED MECHANICALLY rather than from the analysis list - `grep -rn "isEmpty then [0-9]" */src/main` - which found 16 sites including two the list did not name. Those two nearly cost me a bad escalation: hsmm.scala:665 and :673 set a transition probability to 1.0 on empty sources, in the inference engine itself, which reads far worse than anything in the bead. THEY ARE CORRECT. When sources is empty the map over it is empty, so the log(1.0 - pIn) inside is never evaluated, and external states correctly receive all the mass - you cannot transition to a source state that does not exist. Forced, not chosen. I checked before writing, which is the only reason I am reporting a negative result instead of a second retraction.

Likewise StorySourceView.scala:236: its 0.0 is followed immediately by `.filter(_._3 > 0.0)`, so the zero is a DELETE-SENTINEL, not a published value.

2. THE REAL TARGET IS TWO SITES, both in cost.scala: dSens 0.0 (absence as a perfect sensory match) and dEnt 0.5 (unspecified entities as mid-agreement). Both already have open beads awaiting YOUR ruling because they move published alignments. So the sweep's inference third is the work you already have queued, and the other thirteen sites are either correct, conservative, or reporting-only.

3. THE FINDING GETS STRONGER, NOT WEAKER, and this is the part I would put in the policy. The bead proved absence-of-convention with two adjacent pairs. The full table proves it harder: the codebase contains FIVE distinct meanings for an empty-guard constant - forced (hsmm), delete-sentinel (StorySourceView), conservative-as-1.0 (lexicalJaccard, a distance), conservative-as-0.0 (lexicalOverlap, a similarity), and flattering (dSens, dEnt) - and NOTHING AT ANY SITE SAYS WHICH IT IS. That is why two adjacent methods can disagree without anyone noticing.

So my proposed policy does NOT unify the values, which would be wrong - lexicalJaccard's 1.0 and lexicalOverlap's 0.0 are both correct, one being a distance and the other a similarity. It requires each site to DECLARE ITS CLASS. Three of the four classes are then cheap to review and only "substantive default" needs argument, which is exactly the small set you would want to see.

I have touched none of the sites. 46f6b99 landed, thank you. Outstanding from you and none of it blocking me: the two cost-model rulings, the placement threshold, and whether the onboarding sticky should move topic or partly become AGENTS.md rules.
